notes: ACCESS: tier(a) direct HTTP succeeded fully (curl_cffi impersonate=chrome, no cookies/session needed). robots.txt (https://www.dwr.com/robots.txt) has a blanket 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /' (also Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, GPTBot, Google-Extended, meta-externalagent) which blocks tier(c) Claude-in-Chrome only, per project rule; 'User-agent: *' has 'Content-Signal: ai-train=no, use=reference' and 'Allow: /', so plain HTTP fetches (tier a) are permitted and were used exclusively - tier(b)/(c) were never needed. TREE: built from the union of (1) the homepage mega-menu (9 top-level depts: New+Featured, Furniture, Outdoor, Lighting+Fans, Storage, Kitchen+Dining, Bed+Bath, Rugs, Decor, Sale) parsed from the raw SSR HTML nav markup, and (2) sitemap_2-category.xml (1974 en_US category URLs) used to cross-check for missed nodes. QTY: every leaf's quantity came from the exact-match regex data-product-count="N" attribute on that page's <div class="grid-footer"> element (Salesforce Commerce Cloud's own authoritative total-result-count field, independent of pagination/show-more state) - not a manual tile count and not a facet count. Every recorded leaf's <link rel=canonical> and <h1> were checked against the requested URL/nav label before recording; several candidate nav links were found to be vanity-slug aliases whose canonical/h1 resolved to a DIFFERENT already-recorded node with an identical qty (true duplicates, dropped) versus others where canonical pointed elsewhere but h1+qty on the requested URL were genuinely distinct content (kept, using the requested URL, canonical anomaly noted per row where relevant) - e.g. kitchen-dining-storage-buffets-sideboards-cabinets and kitchen-dining-buffets-sideboards both carry a canonical of storage-credenzas-sideboards yet render their own distinct h1 'Buffets, Side Boards + Cabinets' (58) rather than that page's real content ('Credenzas, Buffets + Sideboards', 82) - treated as separate real Furniture-department content and excluded (see below), not merged into the Storage row. HAY: dwr.com's live nav/sitemap show no HAY-branded catalog sections (no 'hay' node anywhere in the mega-menu or the 1974-URL category sitemap) - SR26's absorption of hay.com apparently did not surface a distinct HAY sub-tree on dwr.com's own site as of this research pass, so nothing HAY-specific was found to include. EXCLUDED (not fabricated, deliberately dropped): all 'View All'/'Shop By Collection'/named-collection nodes (e.g. storage-collections, bed-bath-collections, shop-by-collection-*, textiles-passel) per the Collections rule; 'Rugs by Color' facet pages (neutral/multi/grey/blue/green/orange-pink-red) because their h1 stayed the generic 'Rugs' with only the count changing - these are search-refinement views, not real distinct category pages, so they failed the h1-match check; rug-shape-rectangular and rug-shape-narrow because their canonical+h1+qty exactly match already-recorded rug-type-area-rug/rug-type-runners (true duplicates); rug-style-runners and accessories-outdoor-rugs for the same true-duplicate reason (canonical+h1+qty all match rug-type-runners/rug-type-indoor-outdoor); bedding-pillows-throws because it is a vanity alias whose canonical+h1+qty exactly match the accessories-pillows-throws parent, which itself is dropped per the parent-URL rule in favor of its 3 real children (Throw Pillows/Throw Blankets/Seat Cushions); all Furniture-department storage-adjacent nodes that have NO parallel listing inside the dedicated Storage top-nav department (office-credenzas-pedestal-storage, office-shelving/office-file-storage, kitchen-dining-storage-buffets-sideboards-cabinets/kitchen-dining-buffets-sideboards 'Buffets, Side Boards + Cabinets', kitchen-dining-storage-bar-carts-trolleys 'Bar Carts, Trolleys + Cabinets' - sampled product names confirmed these are serving carts/bar cabinets, not general storage) per storage.md Sec21/Sec15/Sec20 (prefer Furniture, or exclude serving carts, when there is no explicit Storage-department placement); non-storage/non-textile Home-Organization siblings (Folding Screen + Room Dividers, Step Stools, Cleaning Tools, Fireplace Tools) per the tools/dividers exclusions; /bath ('Bathroom Decor + Accessories', 31 items) was excluded from both arrays - it has no sub-category split, its own site label is 'Decor + Accessories' (not Storage or Textile), and a product-name sample showed a genuine mix (~2 textile items, a plurality of storage-type items, and several pure-decor items e.g. mirrors/step ladder) with no way to isolate a clean qty for either category; kitchen-dining-table-linens-coaster was KEPT as Textile but flagged LOW/MANUAL REVIEW because its 10-item combined count also includes non-textile coasters and metal napkin rings that cannot be isolated from the site's single total. Also excluded as non-navigable: several sitemap-only nodes (small-spaces-storage, hidden-storage, baby-storage, kids-storage-organization, teen-storage-shelving/accessories/furniture, office-storage) whose own breadcrumbs trace to 'Baby Furniture'/'Kids Furniture'/'Work from Home' sections that are not reachable from any current mega-menu path or footer link (verified zero occurrences of Kids/Teen/Baby/Nursery/Small Spaces anywhere in the live homepage HTML) - treated as legacy/orphaned pages outside the site's actual current navigation rather than part of the live category tree.
